lead: the hospital rang at four in the morning about a woman you had not seen in two years. your name was on a line in her file, in her handwriting, and nobody had ever mentioned it to you.
sun: no request is ever sent. what reaches you is the situation itself — a voicemail with the wrong brightness laid over it, a brother's name coming up twice in one evening, a rent said at a pitch the sentence did not need. you hold the actual state of six or seven lives at any hour, taken off material addressed to somebody else, and each arrangement began before anybody decided to ask.
moon: a thing put down in you meets nothing that would have to be moved first. a coat goes onto an unoccupied chair and nobody asks whose chair it is. so what you heard is yours inside the same hour, and a year on it gets described as the kind of person you have always been — assumption first, deposit second, and by the third winter it is furniture.
pull: your name is on documents you have not read, in houses you have not been inside since the spring, put there by people who were certain you would not mind.
tension: nowhere does the total appear. the woman with the file knows about the file. the man whose son sleeps at yours on wednesdays knows about wednesdays. each is looking at one item, correctly sized, easy to carry, and each is right about their own. the week two of them land at once, the only person holding both is you, and correcting anybody's arithmetic would mean going to a man about a favour he never asked for and does not remember.
cost: people rely on you who have never once checked whether they could, and they are right to — the checking was done years ago, on their behalf, by the one being relied on. nothing about it can be closed, since nobody opened it. the winter your own year went badly, two of them rang inside a week, both about something else, and both correct that the line was open.

lead: an ordinary tuesday goes in whole: the cab radio, the row through the neighbours' wall, your own kitchen at seven. no register anywhere in you was off for any of it, and there is no second setting to go to.
sun: rooms do not adjust for you. people finish sentences in front of you they would swallow in front of anyone else; you register as a place a sentence can go, with no route out the other side. and what the room actually needs gets done inside the week, by you, before the room has words for it, so the account of the evening afterwards has nobody in it doing anything.
moon: nothing runs at a lower gain. the same instrument is up at breakfast, in a queue, in a country whose language you do not have, where the tone arrives without the words. the acting-on runs everywhere, so no part of the life is a holiday from either half, and the closest thing to quiet is being alone, where the last room plays back at the volume it came in at.
pull: you have never sat in a room you could not hear, and never sat in one that could see what you did about what you heard. twice over, with nothing in you set against either.
tension: what people prescribe is a break, kindly, and a week in a borrowed house by the sea comes back at the same level, because the family that went with you was audible for all of it, and so was the couple at the next table. there is no location where the intake runs lower. so the settled description is that nothing bothers you, and the evidence is that you have never come back from anywhere with anything to report.
cost: you can sit through what empties other people — a bedside, a row years in the building, a meeting where a man is politely finished — because none of it has to be worked out there. it arrives already understood, and understood is heavy, never a shock. the nearest thing to being received in a decade was a man who got you badly wrong and would not let it go.

lead: the crew came off the water saying the conditions had been kind. what happened was that you heard something in the breathing behind you at the second bend and took a quarter off the rate without mentioning it.
sun: what comes back off a boat is never only timing. the catch going late by an amount nobody could measure, a breath taken half a stroke early, the particular quiet of a man who has decided to say nothing — it all reaches you from behind, and you never turn around. so by the second lap you have which of them has had a bad week, and roughly what kind of bad, off a sound.
moon: and the only lever in your hands is a number. the rate comes down two, or holds when everything wants it pushed, and four people reorganise around that without a word going anywhere near them. it is an exact instrument for the one thing it does. it can say faster and it can say slower. every response you have ever made to any of them has left you as pace.
pull: you can hear which man is coming apart and you can adjust a number. everything you have done about anybody in that boat went out as tempo, and tempo cannot be addressed to a person.
tension: the one who left the club two winters ago had been getting slower months off you for most of a year, aimed correctly, and never a sentence. he went because nobody had said anything to him, which is accurate. the sentence was available to any of the others; from you it would have arrived as proof he had been discussed. so he got the one thing that could be given without naming him, and it was not enough.
cost: nobody in that crew has had to announce they were struggling in fifteen years. the pace absorbs it, the month passes, and the man keeps his account of himself intact. the week your life went wrong the rate went with it, and the return came off the boat at full volume — the irritation, the joke about your age, the view you had gone soft. you heard all of it.

lead: stay as long as you want, you said, and meant it. that sentence is what he would repeat if anybody asked about that year; the seven months after it were fitted to a state he never once put into words.
sun: he told you it was about the job, and it was about his father, and you had that on the first evening off the way he said the town out loud. none of it can be raised. so it goes into the shape of the arrangement instead — which hour the kitchen is his, the friend not invited while he is here, the question about work that never comes up at breakfast.
moon: room is the one thing that has to be handed over in words. it is accepted out loud or refused to your face, and refusing costs the person worst off more than they can pay. so the size of what you put forward is set by what can be taken, not by what is needed, and the ones furthest down get the smallest version: a night, a lift, a key.
pull: the ones in real trouble get the smallest offer you have. you sized it so it could be refused without costing them a thing, and several of them refused it.
tension: by the fourth month you could hear it was over — the calls had different weather in them, he was arguing about football again — and he stayed because leaving would have conceded there had been something to leave. an open offer has no closing move in it, and the change in his phone voice cannot be produced as a reason without telling him it has been read all year. so the room went on being his for another season.
cost: somebody can be at their worst in your house and not once have to describe what is wrong. the house keeps the shape of them afterwards: a chair where it is because of a man who left in the spring, a shelf in the bathroom untouched for four years for a woman who is well now, in another city. the accommodation outlasts the trouble every time.
